reason: The idea itself holds up: it costs nothing, it is text only, it adds no kernel, slot or finals input, and it is new (grep of CONTEXT for R12P-2 or a whole-history private table: 0 hits; only C1-C4 at l.2288). But the reading rule as written would pre-register wrong contrasts, and fixing them after private scores appear would be post-hoc. (1) WRONG BASES, checked against experiments/lb_poll/ledger.md and the poll.log descriptions. P29 (exp49) and P30 (exp50) are exp39 = P20 (0.947) plus the edge filter, not P28 (P28 = exp48 = exp39 + leaf prune + insertion, 0.948). So 'P28->P29/P30' subtracts the insertion and pushes H-T toward a pass. P12 is itself a z-flip arm (exp30 + Z-flip, base P11 0.944 -> 0.941), and P16 is the clean z-flip re-test on exp29 realised (base P14 0.947 -> 0.938). So 'P12->P16' compares two z-flip arms on different primaries and means nothing. The correct pairs are P11->P12 and P14->P16. The axis-flip base is P14 (exp29), not 'P29-base'. (2) SIGN BUG: if the insertion hurt on private (sum < 0), r_priv < 0, 0.002/r_priv < 0, and the clip to [+0.004, +0.02] returns +0.004, the most lenient bar. A zero sum with non-zero parts (e.g. -1/0/+1) divides by zero, and the 'all 0' clause does not cover that case. (3) r_priv MEASURES ROUNDING, NOT TRANSFER: the denominator is 0.0149 and each displayed delta has a rounding error in (-1, +1) thousandths, so the sum can be off by up to 3 thousandths, i.e. r +-0.2, against a true r of ~0.07-0.2. The possible values 0/.067/.134/.201/.268 map to bars .02/.02/.015/.010/.0075, so the bar is set by which way the 3 dp rounding falls. The denominator also mixes a 199-video CONFIRMATION delta (+0.0019, CONTEXT l.1306) with the exp60 ins35 6bba-only number (+0.0065), which results.md l.74 labels an IN-SAMPLE UPPER BOUND (the pooled figure is ~+0.0063). The K2-stack +0.0065 was never measured; it is borrowed. P34->P35 and P38->P37 are nearly the same stack, so the three pairs are really two independent readings. (4) A KNOWN CONFOUND IS LEFT OUT: #35's latency (6.72, 7.73] h straddles its own 7.5 h x138 deadline (round 12 R12P-1), so a possible degrade can only lower P34->P35, and that bias goes straight into the r_priv numerator. (5) H-T COUNTS A DISPLAYED 0 AS <= 0. All five T items already read 0 or negative on public, so P(pass) is ~0.9 and the test says almost nothing (R12P-1: a displayed 0 carries no information). VALUE: 0 for the competition score, since this is post-deadline calibration only. As written, it would set every post-deadline bar from 3 dp rounding noise.
fix: Append to CONTEXT a corrected rule, text only, before 29 Sep 23:59 UTC. It reports the table and does not compute a bar. PAIRS (base -> arm, from the ledger): E = {P27->P28 insertion (lab +0.0019 CONF), P34->P35 insertion (exp60 ins35 in-sample upper bound, pooled ~+0.0063; carries the #35 degrade flag), P38->P37 insertion (no K2 lab; borrowed), P28->P31 head}. T = {P20->P29 edge filter (+0.0162), P20->P30 ef_a0 (+0.0095), P14->P20 DNVETO (+0.0023), P11->P12 and P14->P16 z-flip, P14->P19 axis-flip, P14->P21/P22/P23 relink family}. N = {P31->P32, P28->P33 float; P35->P36 leaf prune (degrade flag)}. READING: only non-zero displayed deltas count (a displayed 0 carries no information). H-E = at least 2 of the non-zero E deltas are > 0 and none is < 0. H-T = among the non-zero T deltas, the ones < 0 outnumber the ones > 0, and it is NOT READ if fewer than 3 are non-zero. Report the insertion transfer as an INTERVAL: r in [(S-k)/D, (S+k)/D], where S = the sum of the displayed deltas in thousandths, k = the number of pairs and D = the lab sum, computed both with and without P34->P35. Set the post-deadline bar only as: if the lower end of the interval > 1/6, bar = 0.002/lower end (floor 0.004); if the upper end < 1/6, or S <= 0, bar = +0.02 (or 'learning only'); otherwise keep 1/6 (bar +0.012). Never divide by S <= 0. Calibration only, never a finals input.
realistic_gain: 0 on the competition score (post-deadline calibration; no finals input). The corrected table gives a sign-level read on about 10 contrasts over the multi-embryo private split. An r estimate is identifiable only as a wide interval (about +-0.1..0.2), so it can confirm or overturn the 1/6 rule only at the extremes. Cost ~0.5 eng-h of text now and ~2 h on 30 Sep.
